questions.q: Why does the Orbis Industrial design use Enterprise Territory Management rather than role hierarchy as the structural backbone for Opportunity sharing?
options: Access genuinely follows territory (geographic/vertical) assignment rather than a management reporting line, so territory management matches the real shape of the business
Role hierarchy cannot be used alongside sharing rules
Territory management is required for any object over 1 million records
Role hierarchy does not support external users
questions.explain: The lesson's principle is to pick the mechanism matching the real access pattern; since Orbis's access boundary is territory, not org-chart management, territory management avoids faking that structure with a role hierarchy.

questions.q: How is the Named Account Manager requirement (accounts spanning multiple territories) handled in the design?
options: By restructuring the entire territory model to accommodate each named account
By switching the OWD to Public Read/Write for all Opportunities
By giving every Named Account Manager the System Administrator profile
By a criteria-based sharing rule layered on top of the territory baseline, as a narrow, deliberate exception
questions.explain: Rather than abandoning the territory backbone for everyone, a targeted sharing rule grants the specific named-account exception on top of it.

questions.q: Which mechanism scopes each Partner Community user to only their own partner organization's Opportunities?
options: Apex managed sharing
Manual sharing
Sharing Sets
Restriction Rules
questions.explain: Sharing Sets are the mechanism designed specifically for scoping external/community users' access to records associated with their own account or organization.

questions.q: How does the design satisfy EMEA's requirement that a data protection office can list exactly who has access to its country's records on demand?
options: By building a separate EMEA-only sharing mechanism not used elsewhere
By disabling all sharing rules for EMEA records
By keeping every sharing grant's Row Cause distinct and nameable, so a query against the Share object grouped by Row Cause answers the question directly
By manually maintaining a spreadsheet of EMEA access outside Salesforce
questions.explain: The design applies a global discipline (clean, distinct Row Causes) rather than inventing a region-specific mechanism, making the requirement answerable by query anywhere, including EMEA.

questions.q: What operational practice addresses leadership's concern about the twice-yearly territory restructuring taking hours to recalculate?
options: Switching Opportunity's OWD to Public Read/Write during restructuring
Using Defer Sharing Calculations as a planned part of the restructuring window, per Lesson 16's recommended pattern
Deleting all sharing rules before each restructuring
Restructuring territories one Account Executive at a time to avoid any batch change
questions.explain: A bulk, predictable territory restructuring is exactly the scenario Defer Sharing Calculations is built for: suspend recalculation during the batch of changes, then resume once, rather than recalculating after every intermediate step.
